standard.title: Community participation
standard.description: why people participate within communities and how students can actively participate and contribute to communities
standard.strand: Knowledge and Understanding — Civics and Citizenship
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 civics context: Students have explored rules and authority (AC9HS3K06). No direct prior standard on participation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain why people participate in communities and describe how they can actively contribute.

nodes.label: Why people participate in communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify groups that participate in the local community, describe their purpose and explain why individuals choose to contribute.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two community groups and explain why each participates or contributes.
nodes.typical_width: Identify groups that actively participate in the local or virtual community and explore their purpose; investigate the motivations of individuals who contribute (volunteers, leaders, Elders); examine how individual contributions can be recognised.
wider: Investigate how an individual's contribution has been officially recognised (e.g. Order of Australia) and what criteria are used
Explore how online and virtual communities enable participation beyond geographic boundaries
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding motivation for participation is prerequisite to students identifying their own possible contribution — without understanding why others participate, proposals for own participation lack rationale.

response_modes.reason: Diverse examples of participation (volunteering, cultural leadership, community service) give richer understanding than a single type.

success_criteria: Names at least two community participation groups
Explains why individuals participate in each

nodes.label: How students can participate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe ways they could participate in a school or community project and explain what contribution they could make.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one specific way they could contribute to a school or community project and explain what the contribution would involve.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how they could participate in a school or community project (raising money for aid, protecting a bird habitat, community clean-up); identify resources needed; connect participation to community benefit.
wider: Develop an action plan for a class participation project including roles, resources and expected outcomes
Investigate how a student-led initiative has made a difference in a community and discuss what made it successful

response_modes.reason: Student participation proposals integrate community knowledge, civic motivation understanding and personal agency — the integration of civics knowledge into action.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one way they could contribute to a community project
Explains what the contribution would involve and who it would benefit
